Dialog.BatmanAc.Body.Intro: HDR for the game's DirectX 11 renderer by boostedwarr, with optional DLAA or FSR anti-aliasing at native resolution. The game is 32-bit, so the anti-aliasing runs in a small 64-bit helper program that the mod starts by itself.
Dialog.BatmanAc.Body.Also:
•  Install the mod's helper (renodx-batmanac-dlaa-host64.exe) next to it
  •  Add the newest DLSS (nvngx_dlss.dll) for DLAA and AMD's FSR files for FSR
  •  Set the launcher's options the mod needs: DirectX 11, MSAA off, FXAA off, Depth of Field on
Dialog.BatmanAc.Body.InGame:
•  Turn Anti-Aliasing on in the mod's settings (ReShade menu) once you're in the game, not at the main menu: it can fail to start there and then stays off until the game restarts
  •  Leave the brightness slider at its default and use the mod's Game Brightness instead
  •  Keep MSAA and FXAA off and Depth of Field on in the launcher (use the mod's Depth of Field slider for less blur)
  •  The game runs borderless; the mod needs that for HDR
Dialog.BatmanAc.Body.Remove: Removing the mod removes the helper, DLSS and FSR files. The launcher options stay as they are.

Dialog.Dxvk.WarningContent:
⚠ ADVANCED FEATURE — USE AT YOUR OWN RISK

DXVK is an unofficial DirectX-to-Vulkan translation layer.
No support will be provided if a game is not compatible.

WHO SHOULD USE THIS:
• Primarily benefits older DX8/DX9 games (e.g. FFXIV, Morrowind)
• Enables ReShade compute shaders on games that don't support them natively
• Can reduce CPU-bound stuttering in older titles

IMPORTANT WARNINGS:
• Anti-cheat games may ban players using DXVK
• Game overlays (Steam, NVIDIA, RTSS) may conflict or stop working
• Exclusive fullscreen is blocked — use borderless windowed
• First launch will be slow due to shader compilation (improves on subsequent runs)
• Some games may crash or have graphical glitches with DXVK

Do you want to continue?
Dialog.DxvkInfo.Content:
DXVK translates DirectX 8/9/10/11 API calls into Vulkan.

Benefits:
• Enables ReShade compute shaders on older DX games
• May improve performance and reduce shader stutter
• Enables HDR output via dxvk.conf
• Borderless fullscreen recommended over exclusive fullscreen

⚠ Anti-cheat games may ban players using DXVK.
⚠ Game overlays (Steam, NVIDIA, RTSS) may conflict.

Dialog.FullRefresh.Content:
This will clear all caches and re-scan everything from scratch:

• Re-detects all games from every storefront
• Re-scans DLSS/Streamline DLL paths
• Re-detects graphics APIs and engine types
• Rebuilds shader and addon deployment state

Try a normal Refresh first — it handles most issues without the full rescan, and fully rescans the selected game (DLSS added or removed, for example). Use Full Refresh as a last resort if games are missing, paths have changed, DLSS has been added to a game, or the DLSS section is missing from a game card.

The next couple of restarts may take a few seconds longer while caches are rebuilt.

Do not close RHI while the refresh is in progress — closing early will result in a missing library and the scan will need to be repeated.

Faq.Body.AddingGamesManually: If a game isn't detected, click the green + next to the search box and choose its .exe, or drag the .exe onto the RHI window. RHI adds it to your library and detects its engine.
Faq.Body.ChooseShaders:
Click 'Shaders/Addons' in the toolbar, then 'Global Shaders'. Lilium's HDR shaders are selected by default. Your selection is deployed to every game with ReShade.

Expand a pack to pick individual shaders, or search for one. Use the Profiles panel to save named selections, and Export to copy one as a zip you can paste into Discord.
Faq.Body.DlssStreamline:
Games with DLSS or Streamline files have a DLSS / Streamline section. Pick a version for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, Frame Generation, Neural Rendering or Streamline, and RHI swaps the file. Originals are backed up: choose 'Default' or click Restore DLSS/SL to put them back.

You can also set presets and render scale per game. These are written to the NVIDIA driver, so you don't need NVIDIA Profile Inspector.
Faq.Body.DofFix: DOF Fix backports a depth-of-field fix from Unreal Engine 5.7 to games on UE 5.0–5.6. When a game supports it, it appears under Recommended in the Components section. Install it alongside RenoDX for the best result.
Faq.Body.FrameLimiters: ReLimiter and Display Commander are ReShade addons that limit frame rate precisely, which is ideal for VRR displays. Install one of them (not both) from the Components section. ReLimiter is recommended. Set your target FPS in Settings → Components, per game in the ReLimiter ⚙, or in-game.
Faq.Body.FullRefresh: If games are missing, a game has moved, or DLSS files were added or removed, use 'Full refresh' in Settings → Tools & Maintenance to rescan everything from scratch.
Faq.Body.InstallReShade: ReShade is needed for RenoDX, Luma, frame limiters and DOF Fix. Click 'Install ReShade' in the Components section. RHI picks the right file name for the game's graphics API and installs the version with addon support.
Faq.Body.Luma:
Luma is a mod framework by Pumbo. Depending on the game, a Luma mod may add HDR, DLSS, DLAA or rendering fixes. Check the Info button to see what each mod offers.

• Named mods: for supported games, shown on the Luma row. Mods only on Nexus Mods open their Nexus page.
• Generic Luma: for DX11 Unreal Engine games. RHI applies the Engine.ini tweaks and launch arguments listed on the Luma wiki.

Generic Luma can be used alongside RenoDX. Named Luma mods normally replace RenoDX.
Faq.Body.NvidiaDriverSettings: The Driver Settings section changes the game's NVIDIA profile directly. It needs Admin Mode (Settings → General → Admin Mode).
Faq.Body.OptiScaler:
OptiScaler lets a game's DLSS, FSR or XeSS inputs drive a different upscaler (FSR, XeSS, DLSS), and can add or replace frame generation on any GPU. It's in the Extras section.

Before installing, set your GPU type (and DLSS inputs for AMD/Intel) in Settings → Components → OptiScaler. Then choose a variant in the OptiScaler ⚙:
• Stable: official release.
• Nightly: latest build, or pin a specific build.
• DLSS NR and F5 DLSSNR: forks with DLSS Neural Rendering.

The ⚙ also sets the upscaler, frame generation, Reflex, DLSS presets, render scale, Engine.ini fixes and Neural Rendering options, and saves presets you can apply to other games.
Faq.Body.RenoDX:
RenoDX mods give games true HDR output. The RenoDX HDR row shows what's available for the game:

• Named mods: game-specific HDR mods made by the community.
• UE-Extended: for Unreal Engine games without a named mod.
• Generic Unity: for Unity games without a named mod.

A ✓ next to the installed mod means it's complete; a hammer means it's still in progress. Click 'Available Mods' in the toolbar to see every game with a RenoDX, Luma or Ultra+ mod.
Faq.Body.SelectGame:
Your games are listed on the left. Click a game to open its detail panel. Use the search box and the filter chips (All Games, Installed, Favourites, Unreal, Unity, RenoDX, Luma…) to find games.

The detail panel is split into sections: Components, Game Overrides, Neural Rendering, DLSS / Streamline, Driver Settings, Management and Extras. Click a section heading to collapse it, or drag its ≡ handle to reorder.
Faq.Body.Settings: Click 'Settings' in the toolbar for options that apply to all games:
Faq.Body.SystemTray: RHI can keep running in the system tray when you close the window. Right-click the tray icon to launch recent games without opening RHI.
Faq.Body.UpdatingEverything: Click 'Update All' in the toolbar to update ReShade, RenoDX, ReLimiter, Display Commander, OptiScaler, RE Framework, DXVK, Luma and DOF Fix across all your games.
Faq.Body.VulkanGames: Vulkan games (shown with a VLK badge) use a global ReShade layer installed to C:\ProgramData\ReShade. This needs administrator rights, so RHI asks for permission the first time.
Faq.Body.WelcomeToRhi: RHI finds the games on your PC and installs, updates and removes HDR mods, ReShade, shaders, frame limiters, DLSS files and more, and manages your NVIDIA driver settings, all from one place. Here's how to get started.

Faq.Tip.AddingGamesManually:
Wrong folder? Use Management → Change install folder.
Manually added games can be removed with Management → Reset / Remove game.
Faq.Tip.ChooseShaders:
Per-game shaders: Game Overrides → Shaders → Select.
Your own shaders: click Open Custom Folder in the picker's Profiles panel and put them there. They appear under Custom Shaders.
Global Addons, in the same toolbar menu, manages ReShade addons for all games.
Faq.Tip.DlssStreamline:
NVIDIA Override in the version list tells the driver to use its newest DLSS file instead.
Set your preferred versions and presets once in Settings → DLSS / Streamline → Configure Defaults, then use Quick Apply on any game, or Batch Deploy for many games at once.
DLSS section missing? Use Full refresh in Settings → Tools & Maintenance.
Faq.Tip.DofFix:
DOF Fix only appears on 64-bit UE 5.0–5.6 games.
If a game's engine badge just says 'Unreal Engine', click the badge to mark it as Unreal Engine 5.
Faq.Tip.FrameLimiters:
Installing either limiter turns off the NVIDIA driver frame limit for that game.
VRR cap presets by refresh rate (a little below max keeps VRR active):
• 60Hz → 59 FPS
• 120Hz → 116 FPS
• 144Hz → 138 FPS
• 165Hz → 157 FPS
• 240Hz → 224 FPS
• 360Hz → 324 FPS
These values are pre-configured in RHI's FPS dropdowns.
Faq.Tip.FullRefresh:
Downloads or update checks failing? Add a GitHub token (Settings → Accounts & Data).
To report a problem, click Copy logs in Settings → Tools & Maintenance and/or Copy Report in the game's Management section, then paste it into Discord.
Faq.Tip.InstallReShade:
Change the ReShade version per game in Game Overrides → ReShade Channel: Stable, Nightly, Custom (your own DLL), No Addons or Legacy.
The ReShade ⚙ deploys reshade.ini or ReShadePreset.ini, sets per-game hotkeys, and can stop RHI changing this game's reshade.ini.
Drag a ReShade preset (.ini) onto RHI to install it, along with the shaders it needs.
Faq.Tip.Luma:
Luma needs ReShade. The install button shows 'ReShade required' until it's installed.
The Luma ⚙ (Unreal games) has HDR on First Boot and TAA settings.
Launch arguments such as -dx11 are added on install and removed on uninstall. They only apply when you launch the game through RHI.
DX9 Luma mods get dgVoodoo2 installed automatically.
Faq.Tip.NvidiaDriverSettings: Global defaults (shader cache, G-Sync, FPS limit, VSync, Power Mode, ReBAR) and profile backup/restore are in Settings → Driver Settings. Digital Vibrance is in Settings → Display & HDR.
Faq.Tip.OptiScaler:
OptiScaler and ReShade can run together. If a game crashes with both, give ReShade a different name in Game Overrides → DLL naming overrides.
'Replace with a fresh copy...' in the ⚙ resets the game's OptiScaler.ini from your template.
Faq.Tip.RenoDX:
The RenoDX ⚙ has per-game peak brightness, UE-Extended and Engine.ini HDR options, compatibility settings, and preset export/import.
No mod for your game? Turn on RTX HDR (NVIDIA) or Auto HDR (Windows 11, any GPU) from the same ⚙. Either one replaces RenoDX for that game.
Got an .addon64 from the RenoDX Discord? Drag it onto RHI and pick the game.
Faq.Tip.SelectGame:
Double-click a game to launch it. Right-click a game to open its folder, favourite or hide it, or create a desktop shortcut.
The HDR and RES buttons next to Launch turn Windows HDR on and switch resolution while the game is running.
Type a search, then click the + that appears to save it as a filter chip.
Faq.Tip.SystemTray:
Turn on Close to Tray, Recent Games and Start with Windows in Settings → General → Windows.
Recent Games also appear in the taskbar jump list.
While running, RHI checks for updates every hour with a GitHub token (Settings → Accounts & Data), or every 4 hours without one.
Faq.Tip.UpdatingEverything:
Games with updates show a green dot in the sidebar.
Choose what Update All includes in Settings → General → Components to check, or per game in Game Overrides → Update Inclusion.
Turn on Automatic updates in Settings → General to install updates in the background.
The Updates button at the bottom right shows everything that has been updated.
Faq.Tip.VulkanGames:
All Vulkan games share the same ReShade, so changing the ReShade channel on one changes it for all.
RenoDX addons and shaders are still installed to each game's own folder.
Games that support both DirectX and Vulkan: choose one in Game Overrides → Graphics API.

Info.DisplayCommander: Display Commander is a frame limiter that works alongside ReShade to reduce input lag and improve frame pacing.
Info.Luma: Luma is an alternative HDR mod framework that provides native HDR output for supported games, bypassing the need for ReShade-based injection.
Info.OptiScaler: OptiScaler is an upscaling compatibility layer that enables FSR, XeSS, or DLSS across different GPU vendors, allowing you to use any upscaler regardless of your hardware.
Info.ReFramework: RE Framework is a modding framework for RE Engine games. It enables ReShade injection and other mods by hooking into the game's rendering pipeline.
Info.ReLimiter: ReLimiter is a frame limiter that works alongside ReShade to reduce input lag and improve frame pacing in games.
Info.ReShade: ReShade is a post-processing injector that adds visual effects to games. It is required by RenoDX to apply HDR tone mapping and color grading.
Info.RenoDX: RenoDX is an HDR mod framework that upgrades SDR games to HDR using ReShade. It provides per-game tone mapping and color space conversion.
Info.UeExtended: This game is set to use UE-Extended. It is automatically configured to use native HDR and an Engine.ini will be automatically deployed upon installation. If there is an ingame HDR option then enable that too.

Settings.Dldsr.Info.Description:
DLDSR (Deep Learning Dynamic Super Resolution) renders games at higher resolutions and downscales with AI for sharper image quality. This feature lets you switch DLDSR presets without opening NVIDIA Control Panel.

DLDSR uses a Lanczos algorithm — less jaggies, more stable, but can look slightly painterly. Standard DSR uses a Gaussian filter — more natural but with more aliasing. DLDSR is generally sharper than DSR at equivalent settings.

Recommended factors: DLDSR 2.25x offers the best balance of quality and performance. DSR 4.00x uses significantly more VRAM. DLDSR 1.78x is the most VRAM-friendly option.
Settings.Dldsr.Info.SetupSteps:
1. Open NVIDIA Control Panel → Manage 3D Settings → Global Settings
2. Find "DSR - Factors" and enable the DLDSR factors you want (e.g. 1.78x DL, 2.25x DL)
3. Click Apply and wait for the ~15 second display blackout
4. Come back here and click "Capture Current" to save this state
5. Repeat steps 2-4 for each DLDSR configuration you want to save (e.g. "Off", "2.25x only", "1.78x + 2.25x")
Settings.Dldsr.Info.SmoothnessDescriptio:
Controls the sharpening/smoothing applied during downscale. 100 = no sharpening (pure Lanczos downscale). Lower values add sharpening — the image gets progressively sharper as you reduce it.

Recommended DLDSR smoothness values (from r/MotionClarity):
  • 100 — No sharpening
  • 80 — Sharp without artifacts
  • 75 — Clear
  • 65 — Clearer
  • 55-65 — Similar clarity to DSR 4.00x at 0% (recommended range)
  • 45 — As sharp as DSR 4.00x everywhere

Note: DLDSR uses a Lanczos algorithm — it is naturally much sharper than standard DSR (Gaussian), so it requires higher smoothness values for a comparable look.

Changing smoothness causes the same ~15 second display blackout as applying a full state. Tip: set smoothness first, then click Apply — both will apply together in a single restart.

Setup.Description:
RHI can manage ReShade across all your games automatically. Here's what that includes:

  - Installs and updates ReShade for each game with one click
  - Keeps the correct DLL name per game based on what the game needs
  - Manages shader packs globally - install once, deployed to every game automatically
  - Backs up any shaders already in your game folders before taking over
  - Keeps ReShade in sync when you install RenoDX, OptiScaler, or other components

If you already have a custom ReShade setup - specific shader collections, hand-tuned configs, or a version you prefer - choose "I'll manage it myself" and RHI will leave ReShade completely alone.

Extras.Rtx40Mfg.ReShadeWarning.Content:
ReShade is installed in this game. Universal MFG Unlocker's XeSS frame generation ("XeMFG standalone" in its menu) doesn't start while ReShade is loaded: the mod's menu shows "Waiting menu_factory_not_dxgi". This happens whether ReShade is installed as a DLL or as an ASI.

DLSS multi frame generation works as normal. To use XeMFG with ReShade, install OptiScaler (nightly, F5 or DLSS NR) and set FG Output to XeFG in OptiScaler's settings; RHI then installs the mod as an OptiScaler plugin.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.ReShadeWarning.Title: XeMFG and ReShade
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Tooltip.PluginReinstall: Reinstall Universal MFG Unlocker (loaded by OptiScaler from {0})
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Tooltip.PluginMoveReinst: Reinstall Universal MFG Unlocker. OptiScaler is installed, so it moves from {0} into OptiScaler\plugins.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Tooltip.PluginInstall: Install Universal MFG Unlocker as an OptiScaler plugin (OptiScaler\plugins\MFGUnlocker.asi), as its author recommends with OptiScaler.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.Intro: Press Backspace in-game to open the Universal MFG Unlocker menu. It offers these modes:
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.ModeFollowGame: • Follow game: uses the game's own MFG setting
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.ModeFixed: • Fixed 2x to 6x: forces a specific multiplier
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.ModeDynamic: • Dynamic: targets the display refresh rate or a custom FPS value
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.PresetNote: If the picture freezes above 2x, try Frame Generation preset B, in the mod's menu or in this game's DLSS / Streamline section (on RTX 30, restart the game after changing it).
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.OsIntro: OptiScaler loads the mod as a plugin, as its author recommends. Frame generation is chosen in OptiScaler, not here: open OptiScaler's ⚙ and set FG Output to DLSSG for DLSS multi frame generation, or XeFG for XeMFG. OptiScaler's default (Auto) runs no frame generation.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.OsNote: With a recent OptiScaler nightly (4 November 2026 or newer) the DLSS presets and DLSS 5 are in an "MFG Unlocker" tab of OptiScaler's menu; older builds show the mod's menu beside OptiScaler's. If OptiScaler is removed, RHI moves the mod back next to the game's exe.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.XessViaOs: Through OptiScaler, XeMFG is OptiScaler's FG Output set to XeFG. It uses the XeSS files OptiScaler installs, so nothing else is needed.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.XessIntro: The mod can also run Intel's XeSS frame generation itself, 2x to 6x on any GPU (experimental, DirectX 12 and Vulkan). Tick XeMFG standalone in the in-game menu and pick the MFG mode. In games with DLSS Frame Generation, turn that on in the game; XeMFG replaces it. Other games need DLSS, XeSS or FSR 3.1 upscaling on (Vulkan: DLSS only), with the game's own FSR or XeSS frame generation off.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.XessMissing: XeSS files: missing. Reinstall the mod to add them.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.ReShadeDxgiWarn: ReShade is installed as dxgi.dll in this game. With XeMFG at 5x and 6x, some generated frames may not reach the screen. If that happens, give ReShade a different DLL name in Game Overrides › DLL naming overrides.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Title: 20/30 FG Unlock Settings
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Intro: These settings are saved in the game's dlssg_sm86.ini. Exit the game completely and start it again for changes to apply. Needs NVIDIA driver R580 or newer; on older drivers the mod turns itself off. Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling must be on in Windows (Settings › System › Display › Graphics), or the game's frame generation option stays greyed out.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.NotInstalled: Install 20/30 FG Unlock on this game to change these settings.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Saved: Saved {0}. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.FrameGeneratio: Off leaves the game's own DLSS Frame Generation untouched (no FG on RTX 20/30) without uninstalling.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Engine.Label: Engine
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Engine.Help: DLSS uses NVIDIA's frame generation model. XeSS uses Intel's model: up to 4X, uses about 0.5 GB more video memory, and on RTX 30 is faster at 1440p and below but slower at 4K. It doesn't work with HDR (16-bit) output, and a game it can't handle closes instead of falling back to DLSS.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.MaxFrames.Help: The multiplier the mod tells the game it supports. The game's own menu can still pick a lower one. 6X only works in games that offer 6X or Dynamic multi frame generation; games whose own frame generation stops at 4X stay at 4X.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.XessMaxFrames: XeSS goes up to 4X. Switch Engine to DLSS for 5X or 6X.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Preset.Label: Preset
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Preset.Help: A is the default. B cleans up the HUD in generated frames, but only works if the game provides the extra images (most don't). C is FG Lite: much cheaper to run, slightly lower quality.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.SpeedTier.Help: How far the image may differ from NVIDIA's official output. Exact tiers match it bit for bit; Fast and Fastest are a few percent quicker with tiny differences.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.SuperResolutio: RTX 20/30 only. Pins DLSS preset M or L. INT8 uses the mod's faster kernels: quicker in Performance and Ultra Performance, slower than the game's default in Quality, Balanced and DLAA. No effect while Ray Reconstruction is on.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Engine.Label: Engine
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Engine.Help: Game keeps the game's own frame generation. XeFG replaces the game's DLSS frame generation with Intel XeSS frame generation. DLSS-FG replaces a game's own Intel frame generation with DLSS frame generation; it uses Fixed mode (Game decides runs it at 2x, Dynamic isn't available). For games that ship no frame generation, turn on Frame generation under Games without DLSS; Game or DLSS-FG then adds DLSS Frame Generation, XeFG adds Intel XeFG. Don't combine XeFG with Neural Rendering or Smooth Motion. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Mode.Label: Mode
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Mode.Help: Game decides: the game (or NVIDIA Profile Inspector) chooses the multiplier. Fixed: the multiplier next to it. Dynamic: frame generation adapts toward a target frame rate (the monitor's refresh rate by default).
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Multiplier.Hel: Used in Fixed mode. 5x and 6x are experimental. On an 8 GB card, 2x or 3x is the safer starting point.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DLSSFGpreset.H: Game: no override. A and B use normal frame generation; C uses the faster Lite mode (with some image-quality trade-offs) and needs DLSS FG 310.9.16. Lite doesn't use Frame protection, Protection tuning or the HUD/UI options. B needs the game's HUD-less inputs. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Flipmeteringby: Streamline paces the generated frames itself instead of NVIDIA's flip metering. Try it when 3x or 4x looks choppy while 2x is smooth. Restart the game to apply.
1 to 1000 FPS, or 0 for no RTX Encore limit. Applied through Reflex, or through XeLL with XeFG (needs a restart then). Paused in Dynamic mode. Generated frames may count toward the limit. Press Enter or click away to save.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DynamictargetF: Used in Dynamic mode: the frame rate frame generation adapts toward. 0 follows the refresh rate of the monitor showing the game. Press Enter or click away to save.
Lets Dynamic mode go up to 5x and 6x (needs plenty of VRAM). Off: Dynamic stays at 4x or less.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NVIDIATensorCo: Runs XeFG on NVIDIA Tensor Cores. DirectX 12, RTX 30, 40 and 50 on NVIDIA driver 621.01 or the 621.12 hotfix; only the RTX 4090 has been tested in games. If it can't be used, standard XeFG runs instead; if it fails while running, restart the game.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Variablepacing: Paces XeFG above 2x using the game's real frame timing. Off can make multipliers above 2x unavailable. Restart the game to apply.
Interpolate: the HUD is generated along with the scene. Game layers: uses the game's separate HUD-less and UI images, when the game provides them. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.UIalpha.Label: UI alpha
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.UIalpha.Help: How the game's UI layer stores transparency, for Game layers. Leave Unknown unless you know it: Unknown never guesses and doesn't use UI layers. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Highmultiplier: Keeps generated frames clean from 3x to 6x. Leave on. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Frameprotectio: Protects generated frames against tearing on thin geometry (fences, wires, foliage) and ghosting in moving shadows. No effect with the Lite preset (C). Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Fastframegener: Lowers the GPU cost of each generated frame, with the same image. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Protectiontuni: Refined (default) or Classic. No effect with the Lite preset (C). Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.AutoUIrecompos: Turns DLSS FG's UI recomposition on when the game provides HUD-less images, even if the game doesn't ask for it. Off follows the game. Turn it off in No Man's Sky (duplicated generated frames).
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.UIassist.Label: UI assist
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.UIassist.Help: DirectX 12: captures the HUD-less scene and builds the UI layer itself when the game doesn't provide them.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.ForceUIrecompo: Asks DLSS FG to recompose the HUD separately even when the game doesn't request it.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Customrendersc: Render scale in percent (50 to 100) when DLSS render scale is Custom. Press Enter or click away to save.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DLSSrenderscal: Forces the DLSS render resolution. Game: no override. The game must already use DLSS.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Upscaler.Label: Upscaler
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Upscaler.Help: Game keeps the game's DLSS Super Resolution. XeSS replaces compatible DLSS Super Resolution with Intel XeSS. Applies live in DirectX; Vulkan needs XeSS set before the game starts.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.XeSSonTensorCo: Runs XeSS Super Resolution on NVIDIA Tensor Cores (RTX 30, 40 and 50, DirectX 12, driver 621.01 or 621.12; tested on the RTX 4090). Only applies when Upscaler is XeSS. If it can't be used, standard XeSS runs instead; if it fails while running, restart the game. Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.FastSuperResol: RTX 30 only, DirectX 12, DLSS 310.9.x: faster DLSS Super Resolution for presets L and M. No effect with Ray Reconstruction or DLAA. The image is very close to NVIDIA's but not identical. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DLSSSRpreset.H: Game: no override. Applies to all quality modes; which presets work depends on the game's DLSS DLL. A to F are legacy. Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DLSSRRpreset.H: Ray Reconstruction preset. Game: no override. A to C are legacy; F needs nvngx_dlssd 310.9.1 or newer. Doesn't turn RR on. Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.SRHDRinput.Hel: Colour input mode for the upscaler. Game: follow the game. On: HDR linear input. Off: SDR input. Doesn't turn on display HDR. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.SRautoexposure: Upscaler auto exposure. Game: follow the game. Some DLSS presets (L) force it. XeSS auto exposure costs GPU time and isn't recommended for SDR. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.SmoothMotion.H: NVIDIA's driver frame interpolation, also for games without frame generation. RTX 40 and 50: turns on NVIDIA's own Smooth Motion. RTX 30: DirectX 11, 12 and Vulkan. RTX 20 (experimental): DirectX 12, driver 621.01. Needs one of the drivers RTX Encore lists. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.GraphicsAPI.He: The game's graphics API, which Smooth Motion needs to know. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NeuralRenderin: Turns DLSS Neural Rendering on. Needs the NR DLL above. The first launch prepares it in the background. Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NRmodel.Label: NR model
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NRmodel.Help: B (default): smaller and much faster. A: the larger network of NR 310.8.0. Auto: the DLL's choice (B). Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NRprecision.He: RTX 20 and 30: Exact gives the same output as NVIDIA; Fast is quicker with small image differences. No effect on RTX 40 and 50. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NRfastprocessi: RTX 20 and 30: faster Neural Rendering processing with exactly the same output. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.GPUseries.Help: Leave on Auto unless RTX Encore detects your GPU wrongly. Restart the game to apply.

Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.Intro: MFG Unlock unlocks DLSS multi frame generation (3x to 6x) on RTX 40 Series GPUs, brings DLSS frame generation (DLSS-G and XeMFG DLSS-G) to RTX 20 and 30 Series GPUs (experimental), and runs Intel XeSS multi frame generation (XeMFG, 2x to 6x) on RTX 20 to RTX 50 Series GPUs.
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.VulkanWarni: This is a Vulkan game. Vulkan support in MFG Unlock is experimental: DLSS-G and XeMFG DLSS-G need the game's own DLSS frame generation (or Add frame generation), and XeMFG needs the game to use DLSS Super Resolution or Ray Reconstruction. Some Vulkan games also need a launch option before ReShade loads (for example +r_allowBlackListedLayers 1).

XeMFG DLSS-G: Intel's model generates the frames inside the game's DLSS frame generation, 2x to 6x; the mod recommends it for games with DLSS frame generation. XeMFG: Intel's frame generation with its own presentation, 2x to 6x on RTX 20 to RTX 50 Series, for games without DLSS frame generation; it needs borderless or windowed mode. Restart the game after changing this, and turn frame generation on in the game's own menu.

Faq.Body.Extras:
The Extras section holds optional tools:
• Frame gen for any game: RTX Encore (RTX 20–40) and HSF (RTX 40/50, ReShade add-on) add frame generation to games without it.
• Games with DLSS frame gen: DLSS Enabler (any DX12 GPU, including AMD, Intel and GTX), Universal MFG Unlocker (DLSS multi frame gen on RTX 20–40, XeSS frame gen on any GPU), MFG Unlock (RTX 40/50, ReShade add-on) and 20/30 FG Unlock (RTX 20/30, DX12) raise the multiplier or unlock it on other cards.
• ASI Loader: loads .asi plugins.
• DXVK: runs DX8–DX11 games through Vulkan. The Lilium HDR variant gives older games HDR.
• dgVoodoo2: runs DX9 games through DX11.
Faq.Body.NeuralRendering:
The Neural Rendering section installs DLSS 5 neural rendering tools. RHI picks the right method for the game, and installs ReShade too if needed:
• ShortFuse DLSS Tool: most games with native DLSS.
• DLSS5 Tool: DX12 games with native DLSS.
• DLSS5 Tool + DX11 Bridge: DX11 and Vulkan games with native DLSS.
• DLSS5 Feeder: games without DLSS, including OpenGL, DX9 and 32-bit games.

Faq.Bullets.Settings.6: Driver Settings: global NVIDIA driver defaults and profiles

Faq.Tip.Extras: Most of these ask which file name to use when you install them. Names already used by RHI's other components are disabled, and any game file that gets replaced is backed up.
Faq.Tip.NeuralRendering:
Each method's versions, and the NR DLL version, can be pinned or left on Latest.
NR Cost Scaler runs neural rendering at reduced cost. Turn it on before installing. ShortFuse already includes it.
Faq.Tip.WelcomeToRhi: Recommended first step: add a free GitHub token in Settings → Accounts & Data → GitHub token. Without one, GitHub allows only 60 requests an hour, which can make downloads and update checks fail. Create a classic token at github.com/settings/tokens with no boxes ticked, paste it in and click Save.

Settings.SteamGridDb.ApiKeyBox.Tooltip: Paste your SteamGridDB API key, then press Enter or Save. The saved key isn't shown again; paste a new one to replace it.
Settings.SteamGridDb.SaveButton.Tooltip: Check the key with SteamGridDB and save it.
Settings.SteamGridDb.GetFreeApiKey.Toolt: Opens steamgriddb.com. Sign in (with Steam), then generate a key under Preferences › API and paste it above.
Settings.SteamGridDb.Status.NoKey: No key saved. Spotlight's artwork picker shows only the Steam art.
Settings.SteamGridDb.Status.Saved: Key saved. Browse covers and banners from a game's Artwork menu in Spotlight.
Settings.SteamGridDb.Status.BadKey: SteamGridDB didn't accept this key. Check you copied all of it.
Settings.SteamGridDb.Status.Offline: Couldn't reach SteamGridDB to check the key. Check your connection and try again.
Settings.SteamGridDb.Status.Unexpected: SteamGridDB sent an unexpected reply. Try again later.
Settings.Theme.Title: Colour theme
Settings.Theme.Description: Changes RHI's colours. Pick a theme, or Custom to choose your own colours. Changes show straight away.
Settings.Theme.Combo.Tooltip: OLED Black uses a true black background. High Contrast makes text and borders stronger. Colour-blind Friendly uses status colours that stay apart with red-green colour blindness (blue = installed, pink = update, yellow = warning, orange = error).
Settings.Theme.ContrastNote: Text may be hard to read on this background. Pick a lighter text colour or a darker background.
Settings.Theme.Button.StartFromTheme.Too: Replaces your custom colours with a built-in theme's colours.
Settings.Theme.Button.Reset.Tooltip: Sets your custom colours back to RHI's default colours.
Settings.Theme.Button.Share.Tooltip: Copies a code for your colours. Anyone can paste it into Import theme to use them.
Settings.Theme.Button.Import.Tooltip: Paste a theme code someone shared to use their colours. Replaces your custom colours.
Settings.ThemeShare.Copied: Theme code copied. Paste it anywhere to share your colours; others use Import theme to apply it.
Settings.ThemeShare.CopyManually: Copy this code to share your colours; others use Import theme to apply it.
Settings.ThemeShare.ImportHint: Paste a theme code (it starts with RHI-THEME:). It replaces your custom colours.
Settings.ThemeShare.InvalidCode: That isn't a theme code. Copy the whole code, from RHI-THEME: to the last colour.
Settings.UpliftKey.Label: NR on/off key
Settings.UpliftKey.Tooltip:
GITC Uplift's key for turning NR on and off in game (Enable hotkey in Uplift's panel). Click the box and press a key; Backspace or the ↺ button sets it back to None.

RHI writes it into a game's reshade.ini when it installs Uplift there. None leaves the key each game already has.
Settings.UpliftKey.Clear.Tooltip: None (leave each game's own Uplift key alone)
Settings.UpliftKey.WriteAll: Write key to all Uplift games
Settings.UpliftKey.WriteAll.Tooltip: Writes the key into the reshade.ini of every game with GITC Uplift installed by RHI. Skips hidden games and games set to keep their own reshade.ini.
Settings.UpliftKey.PickFirst: Pick a key first. None leaves each game's own Uplift key alone.
Settings.UpliftKey.WrittenOne: Uplift key set to {0} in {1} game.
Settings.UpliftKey.WrittenMany: Uplift key set to {0} in {1} games.
Settings.ShaderCompile.Button.Tooltip: Runs NVIDIA's shader compiler now instead of waiting for the PC to be idle (the NVIDIA App's Compile now). It rebuilds the DirectX 12 shaders your games have already saved in the shader cache for the installed driver, so there's less stutter the first time you play after a driver update. It can't compile games you haven't played (or after Clear shader cache). Uses the Shader pre-compile level above (Medium when it's Off). Takes a few minutes; click again to stop.
Settings.ShaderCompile.Status.NeedsCompi: Needs an NVIDIA driver that includes the shader compiler (NvOSC.exe).
Settings.ShaderCompile.Status.Stopped: Stopped. Shaders already compiled are kept.
Settings.ShaderCompile.Status.CompilerNo: NVIDIA's shader compiler (NvOSC.exe) wasn't found in the installed driver.
Settings.ShaderCompile.Status.StartFaile: NVIDIA's shader compiler couldn't be started. See the log for details.
Settings.ShaderCompile.Status.NothingToC: Nothing to compile. It rebuilds shaders your games have already saved in the shader cache, so it has work to do after you've played games, or after a driver update.
Settings.ShaderCompile.Status.ExitCode: NVIDIA's shader compiler stopped with code {0}. If Shader pre-compile is Off, turn it on and try again.
Settings.ShaderCompile.Status.RunningOur: Compiling shaders. This takes a few minutes and uses some CPU; you can keep using RHI.
Settings.ShaderCompile.Status.RunningOth: NVIDIA's shader compiler is already running (started by the NVIDIA App or its idle task).
Settings.BetaUpdates.Label: Get beta updates
Settings.BetaUpdates.Tooltip:
Betas are test builds of the next RHI version and can have bugs.
With this on, RHI offers each new beta, and moves you to the full release when it's out.
Turning it off doesn't downgrade you: you stay on your beta until the next full release.
Settings.BetaUpdates.Help: Test builds of the next version. You move to the full release when it's out.
Settings.Accounts.PatRejected: GitHub rejected this token (expired or revoked), so RHI isn't using it. Generate a new one and save it here.
Settings.LaunchButtons.Hdr.Tooltip: Show or hide the HDR on launch button on game pages. Hidden, a game's own HDR choice still applies when you launch it from RHI.
Settings.LaunchButtons.Res.Tooltip: Show or hide the Resolution switch button on game pages. Hidden, a game's own resolution choice still applies when you launch it from RHI.
DisplayMode.Item.DlssRrPreset.Label: DLSS Ray Reconstruction preset
DisplayMode.Item.DlssRrPreset.Help: The driver's DLSS Ray Reconstruction preset override for this game (NVIDIA profile). Used in games with ray reconstruction.
DisplayMode.Item.DlssRrScale.Label: DLSS Ray Reconstruction render scale
DisplayMode.Item.DlssRrScale.Help: The driver's DLSS Ray Reconstruction render scale override. Used instead of the Super Resolution one while ray reconstruction is on.
Settings.DisplayModes.Error.CustomReserv: Custom is the name of a game's own mode. Pick another name.
DisplayMode.Dialog.CustomIntro: Make a mode just for this game: tick the settings it changes and set their values. It shows as Custom beside your other modes, only for this game, and wins over them while it's picked.
DisplayMode.Dialog.CustomCreated: Custom mode made. Tick what it changes, then pick Custom as the current mode.
DisplayMode.Dialog.CustomInEffect: The game is in Custom: changes here are written to it now. Settings you don't tick get the game's normal values.
DisplayMode.Dialog.CustomHint: Tick the settings Custom changes and set their values. Settings you don't tick get the game's normal values while it's in Custom. Pick Custom as the current mode above to use it.
DisplayMode.Dialog.DeleteCustomMode.Tool: Removes this game's Custom mode. If the game is in it, its mode is turned off first.
DisplayMode.Dialog.CustomDeletedOff: Custom mode deleted. The game's mode is off: it's back on your global settings.
DisplayMode.Dialog.NotChangedLaunch: Not changed (used when RHI launches the game)
Extras.Hsf.Route.Off: D3D12 routes switched off in HSF.ini
Extras.Hsf.Route.Game: In game: the game's own Streamline
Extras.Hsf.Route.Auto: Picked by HSF (DirectX 9 / 11 / Vulkan games, or not decided yet)

Extras.Hsf.Error.DownloadFailed: Couldn't download HSF. Check your connection and try again.
Extras.Hsf.Error.UnknownLayout: This HSF release has a layout RHI doesn't know yet.

AnrFg.Error.DownloadFailed: Couldn't download ANR FG. Try again later.
AnrFg.Error.CopyFailed: Couldn't copy ANR FG into the game: {0}

Dialog.OptiScaler.AddCustomBuild.Title: Add custom OptiScaler build?
Dialog.OptiScaler.AddCustomBuild.Intro: {0} contains an OptiScaler build. Add it to your custom OptiScaler builds? You can then pick it in a game's OptiScaler settings. RHI never updates custom builds. Only add builds from people you trust.
Dialog.OptiScaler.AddCustomBuild.AddedDe: Added {0}. Pick it in a game's OptiScaler settings (Version), or as the Default version in Settings › Components.
Extras.Bfi.Blocked.Dxvk32Bit: 32-bit games through DXVK can't strobe cleanly (BFI Presenter's own testing). For a 32-bit DirectX 11 game, remove DXVK and use the DX add-on.
Extras.Bfi.Blocked.DirectX8: DirectX 8 games need crosire's d3d8to9 first (the game then runs as DirectX 9 with ReShade as d3d9.dll), or DXVK.
Extras.Bfi.Blocked.DirectX10: The DX add-on covers Direct3D 12, 11 and 9 and OpenGL. DirectX 10 games can use it through DXVK (install DXVK, then BFI Presenter's Vulkan layer).
Extras.Bfi.Blocked.NeedReShade: Install ReShade first: the DX add-on runs inside ReShade (the build with add-on support).
Extras.Bfi.Blocked.NoAddonsChannel: This game uses the "No Addons" ReShade. BFI Presenter needs ReShade with add-on support.
Extras.Bfi.Blocked.OpenGlNeedsNvidia: OpenGL games need an NVIDIA graphics card (BFI Presenter shares their frames through WGL_NV_DX_interop2).
Extras.Bfi.Blocked.ReShadeTooOld: Direct3D 9 games need ReShade 6.8 or newer (this game has {0}).
Extras.Bfi.Error.CopyAddon: Couldn't copy the add-on into the game's ReShade folder. Close the game and check the folder isn't read-only.
Extras.Bfi.Error.Download: BFI Presenter couldn't be downloaded. Check your connection and try again.
Extras.Bfi.Error.LayerAllUsersRights: The layer is still registered for all users: that needs administrator rights.
Extras.Bfi.Error.LayerDownload: The Vulkan layer couldn't be downloaded.
Extras.Bfi.Error.LayerFilesInUse: The Vulkan layer's files are in use. Close any running Vulkan game and try again.
Extras.Bfi.Error.LayerRegisterUser: Couldn't register the Vulkan layer for your Windows user.
Extras.Bfi.Error.LayerUnregisterInUse: The layer was unregistered, but its files are in use. Close any running Vulkan game.
Extras.Bfi.Error.WriteIni: Couldn't put BFIPresenter.ini in '{0}'. Check the folder isn't read-only.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.AllUsers: Also for games run as administrator (asks for administrator rights)
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.AllUsers.Toolti: Windows' Vulkan loader ignores per-user layers in programs run as administrator: User Account Control off, Steam or the game set to run as administrator. Tick this if that applies here.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.AntiCheat: ReShade add-ons and Vulkan layers can count as cheating in online games with anti-cheat. Don't use it there.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.BorderlessNote: Use borderless or windowed mode: exclusive fullscreen isn't supported in DirectX 11 and 9 games.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.DxvkNote: The game runs through DXVK; leave DXVK's frame limit off.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.Flicker: BFI Presenter strobes the screen: it flickers by design. If you're sensitive to flicker or flashing images, take care. Ctrl+Shift+B turns the strobe off while playing.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.FpsLimitOff.Too: Sets Max Frame Rate off for this game (overrides a global limit). Any limiter acting on the game breaks the strobe; BFI Presenter has its own frame cap.
BFI Presenter starts at Gain 0.5, where the lit refresh is unchanged and the picture is half as bright. The author recommends Gain 1.0 for full brightness, especially in HDR. Change it later in the ⚙ or the ReShade overlay.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.GsyncOff.Toolti: Sets G-SYNC off in this game's NVIDIA profile. BFI needs a fixed refresh rate; G-SYNC can pull the display below it.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.Lcd: My display is an LCD (IPS, VA or TN)
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.Lcd.Tooltip: Turns on "LCD: prevent image retention". With BFI every lit refresh gets the same LCD drive voltage, which can leave a ghost image after long sessions. Not needed on OLED.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.PowerMax.Toolti: So the graphics card doesn't clock down between frames (the BFI Presenter Manager offers this at install too).
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.PresentMethod: Vulkan/OpenGL present method: prefer layered on DXGI swapchain
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.PresentMethod.T: Old OpenGL games that present by exchange block the presenter without it (DOOM 3 BFG ran at about 30 fps).
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.Required: Needed in every game: a fixed refresh rate (no G-SYNC / VRR) and no frame limiter on the game (NVIDIA, RivaTuner, ReLimiter, Display Commander). In-game settings are in the BFI Presenter tab of the ReShade overlay.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.RouteDx: BFI Presenter goes next to ReShade as {0}. BFI starts when the game first resizes its window; if it doesn't, change resolution or display mode once.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.RouteVulkan: This is a Vulkan game, so BFI Presenter is installed as its Vulkan layer (once for your Windows user), and BFIPresenter.ini goes next to the game's exe, which switches the layer on for this game only.
Extras.Bfi.InstallDialog.VsyncForceOn.To: Sets Vertical Sync to Force on in this game's NVIDIA profile. Never Force off or Fast Sync with BFI.
Extras.Bfi.NotInstalled.Title: BFI Presenter wasn't installed
Extras.Bfi.Remove.Running: Close the game first: its files are in use.
Extras.Bfi.Remove.Tooltip.Dx: Remove BFI Presenter from this game (the add-on and its BFIPresenter.ini)
Extras.Bfi.Remove.Tooltip.Vulkan: Remove BFI Presenter from this game (deletes its BFIPresenter.ini, which switches the Vulkan layer on here). The layer stays installed for other games; remove it in the ⚙.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.AblGuard.Help: HDR only. OLEDs dim a refresh that puts out too much light overall; the guard lowers the boost in very bright scenes just enough to stay within the panel's limit.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.AblGuard.Label: ABL guard
Extras.Bfi.Settings.AutoFrameCap.Help: At the Refresh rate cap: when the game can't hold the refresh rate, steps down to one game frame per strobe cycle (e.g. 60 at 120 Hz) instead of judder, and back up when it can.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.AutoFrameCap.Label: Automatic frame cap
Extras.Bfi.Settings.DarkFrameFloor.Help: How dark the dark refresh is. 0 = black. 0.05 to 0.15 leaves a faint picture there: less flicker, a bit more blur.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.DarkFrameFloor.Label: Dark frame floor
Extras.Bfi.Settings.DisplayPeak.Help: Your display's real peak brightness (a review such as RTINGS lists it). In HDR the lit refresh never asks for more. 50 to 10000; below 100 the picture is darker than with BFI off. Press Enter or click away to save.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.DisplayPeak.Label: Display peak (nits)
The presenter's own output runs in exclusive fullscreen (the game's window mode is unchanged), so overlays and alt-tab can't hand it to the desktop compositor, where it flickers. Applies at the next game start.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.FixFailed: Couldn't change the NVIDIA profile. Try again, or set it in Driver Settings.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.FixSaved: Saved to the game's NVIDIA profile. Restart the game if it's running.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.FrameGenDll.Help: A loaded frame-generation DLL counts as frame generation on, so the automatic cap stays at Refresh. Off for a game that loads one without using it (BFIPresenterVK.log names it).
Extras.Bfi.Settings.FrameGenDll.Label: Frame generation DLL counts
Extras.Bfi.Settings.FramePacing.Help: Lowest latency (default): always the newest frame. Smooth: every frame shown once, in order, about a refresh more delay; only worth it at Half or Quarter.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.FramePacing.Label: Frame pacing
Extras.Bfi.Settings.FramesPerCycle.Help: Refreshes per flash: 2 = one lit, one dark (a 60 Hz strobe at 120 Hz). More is sharper but darker and flickers more: for 240 Hz and up, with the One game frame per strobe cycle cap.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.FramesPerCycle.Label: Frames per cycle
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Gain.Help: How much of the lost brightness is won back. 0.5 (BFI Presenter's default): the lit refresh as the game drew it, half the average brightness. 1.0 (recommended on bright displays, especially HDR): close to normal brightness.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Gain.Label: Gain
Extras.Bfi.Settings.GameFrameCap.Help: Keeps the game in step with the strobe. Refresh rate (default) with the automatic cap below suits most games, also with frame generation. Half: every frame gets exactly one flash (60 fps at 120 Hz). Quarter: for heavy games. One per strobe cycle: for 240 Hz and up with more frames per cycle.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.GameFrameCap.Label: Game frame cap
Extras.Bfi.Settings.IniVulkan: BFIPresenter.ini in {0} switches the layer on for this game; it must be next to the exe that runs.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.InstallFirst: Install BFI Presenter to change these settings.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Intro: Black frame insertion clocked by the display: sharper motion at a fixed refresh rate. Most settings are also in the BFI Presenter tab of the ReShade overlay{0} Ctrl+Shift+B turns the strobe off.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.DisplayCommand: Display Commander is installed in this game. Make sure its frame limiter is off: BFI Presenter does the pacing.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.FpsLimit: The NVIDIA frame rate limit ({0} fps) acts on the game: use BFI Presenter's own frame cap.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.FpsLimitFixed: The NVIDIA frame rate limit is off for this game.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.FpsLimitGlobal: The NVIDIA frame rate limit ({0} fps, global) acts on the game: use BFI Presenter's own frame cap.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.Gsync: G-SYNC isn't off for this game. It can pull the display below its fixed refresh rate (the overlay warns when VRR takes over).
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.GsyncFixed: G-SYNC is off for this game.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.OptiScaler: OptiScaler's frame rate limit is {0} fps. Set FramerateLimit to 0 in its ⚙: BFI Presenter does the pacing (OptiScaler's frame generation works with it).
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.ReLimiter: ReLimiter is installed in this game. Frame limiters break the strobe: remove it, or set its limit off.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.RtxEncoreFps: RTX Encore's frame limit is {0} fps. Set it to 0 in RTX Encore's ⚙: BFI Presenter does the pacing.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.RtxEncoreSmoot: RTX Encore's Smooth Motion is on. Turn it off for BFI Presenter.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.SmoothMotion: NVIDIA Smooth Motion is on for this game. Turn it off for BFI (the DirectX 11 path stays off while it's active).
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.SmoothMotionFi: Smooth Motion is off for this game.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.VsyncFastSync: Vertical sync is Fast Sync for this game: the strobe loses its cadence.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Issue.VsyncForceOff: Vertical sync is Force off for this game: the strobe loses its cadence.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.LaterRelease.Help: Refresh rate cap, Lowest latency: the game starts each frame as late as safely possible, up to about 5 ms less input delay in light games. Not with frame generation.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.LaterRelease.Label: Later release
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.AllUsers.Toolt: Registers the layer in the machine-wide Vulkan list too (asks for administrator rights).
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.NeedsAllUsers: Games run as administrator (User Account Control off, Steam or the game set to run as administrator) need it for all users too.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.NotChanged: Not changed: it needs administrator rights.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.NotInstalled: The Vulkan layer isn't installed. Installing BFI Presenter in a Vulkan game installs it.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.OrderFixFailed: Not fixed: the all-users list needs administrator rights.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.OrderFixed: BFI Presenter is listed after ReShade now.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.OrderWrong: ReShade is listed after BFI Presenter: fix the load order.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.Remove.Tooltip: Removes the layer from this PC: every Vulkan game stops using it, including games set up with the BFI Presenter Manager.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Layer.Removed: Removed. BFI Presenter no longer runs in any Vulkan game until the layer is installed again.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.LcdPhaseSwap.Help: Turn on for LCD monitors (IPS, VA, TN): with BFI every lit refresh gets the same drive voltage, which can leave a ghost image. Not needed on OLED, or with an odd number of frames per cycle.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.LcdPhaseSwap.Label: LCD: prevent image retention
Extras.Bfi.Settings.LcdSaver.Help: Immediate: every few seconds a short fade to a steady picture while the lit refresh moves. Gradual: the light slides slowly to the other refresh, no fade or stutter (plain strobe only).
Extras.Bfi.Settings.LcdSaver.Label: LCD saver mode
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Method.Help: Variable MPRT (default): dark and mid-tones flash like BFI, highlights too bright for one flash spill into the dark refresh, so brightness is kept. BFI: a truly black dark refresh, sharpest motion, dimmer highlights. Ctrl+Shift+M switches.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.NumberRange: {0} must be a number from {1} to {2}.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Osd.Help: A small panel over the game: frame rate, lost and repeated frames, missed refreshes, a frame-time graph. Ctrl+Shift+F switches.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Osd.Label: On-screen display
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Output.Help: Auto reads SDR or HDR (and which HDR format) from the game. Force it only if colours look clearly wrong.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.PanelBudget.Help: Your display's full-white (100% window) brightness: about 250 for the Sony A95L and similar QD-OLEDs, 150 to 200 for many LG-panel OLEDs. 50 to 1500. Press Enter or click away to save.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.PanelBudget.Label: Panel budget (nits)
Extras.Bfi.Settings.PresenterBuffers.Hel: Real swap-chain buffers behind the presenter. 3 (default) suits most games; 4 gives more slack if it flashes. Applies at the game's next resize.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.PresenterResize.Help: BFI starts when the game first resizes its swap chain. For games that never do (Hades II, Wreckfest 2, Pragmata) the presenter does it after 3 s. Also recreated: for games that recreate their swap chain once at start (Onimusha). If the game freezes or goes black, turn it off and change display mode by hand.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.QueueAhead.Help: Keeps one finished refresh ready, so a busy GPU doesn't cause single flashes (GPU-heavy games). Costs one refresh of latency.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.QueueAhead.Help.Dx: Keeps one present queued, so an occasional late refresh doesn't flash (GPU-heavy and frame-generation games, or when G-SYNC sneaks in). Costs one refresh of latency.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.QueueAhead.Label: Queue one refresh ahead
Extras.Bfi.Settings.RollingScan.Help: Lights the screen in bands from the top down, like a CRT beam, so flicker feels calmer. Meant for 240 Hz and up; at 120 Hz there are two halves with a seam. Ctrl+Shift+S switches.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.RollingScan.Label: Rolling scan
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Running.Dx: The game is running: press Ctrl+Shift+R in the game to reload BFIPresenter.ini. Saving in the overlay overwrites these changes.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.Running.Vulkan: The game is running: the layer picks up changes within a second. Saving in the overlay overwrites them.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SavedReload: Saved. In a running game, press Ctrl+Shift+R to reload.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SdrToHdr.Help: With Windows HDR on, SDR games are sent as HDR10 so the lit refresh has room to get brighter. Turn RTX HDR and Windows Auto HDR off for the game: the conversion should happen once, before the strobe.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SdrToHdr.HelpVulkan: In DXVK games On keeps them SDR (HDR10 hung the NVIDIA driver there); Force in DXVK needs the NVIDIA present method set to Prefer native.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SdrToHdr.Label: SDR to HDR
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SdrWhite.Help: How bright normal white looks in that mode. Match Windows' SDR content brightness (80 + 4 x the slider). Press Enter or click away to save.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SdrWhite.Label: SDR white (nits)
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SettingsFile.Missing: (the add-on creates it the first time the game starts; changes made here go in first).
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SetupOk.Generic: Set a fixed refresh rate (VRR off), VSync on or app-controlled, and no frame limiter for this game.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.SetupOk.Nvidia: No problems found: G-SYNC, VSync and frame limits look right for BFI.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.ShowOverlays.Help: 64-bit DirectX games: lets the RivaTuner OSD and Steam overlay draw on the strobed picture. Steam's overlay crashed some games this way: turn it off if the game crashes. Applies at the next game start.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.ShowOverlays.Label: Show overlays
Extras.Bfi.Settings.TestedNotListed: This game isn't in BFI Presenter's tested-games list yet. The standard setup usually works.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.VulkanLayer.Help: Off keeps the layer out of this game without deleting BFIPresenter.ini.
Extras.Bfi.Settings.VulkanLayer.Label: Vulkan layer in this game
Extras.Bfi.Tooltip:
BFI Presenter by artzox: black frame insertion for sharper motion on fixed-refresh displays (OLED and LCD; built on a 120 Hz OLED, higher refresh rates work too). Variable MPRT keeps full brightness. SDR and HDR. Flickers by design.
Game: needs a fixed refresh rate (G-SYNC / VRR off) and no frame limiter. Works with DLSS, FSR and XeSS frame generation, not Lossless Scaling.
API: Direct3D 12, 11 and 9 and OpenGL (NVIDIA) through a ReShade add-on; Vulkan and DXVK games through a Vulkan layer.

Collections.Manager.MoveUpTooltip: Move this collection earlier in the collection chips.
Collections.Manager.MoveDownTooltip: Move this collection later in the collection chips.

Pcl.Label: PC Latency (PCL)
Pcl.Tooltip:
ReLimiter v4 can show NVIDIA PC Latency (PCL) readings on its overlay.
Windows only allows that when your account is in its Performance Log Users group.
Once it's allowed, RHI turns PCL on in a game's relimiter.ini when it installs ReLimiter v4 there.

Pcl.Dialog.Enable.Title: Allow PC Latency for ReLimiter?
Pcl.Dialog.Disable.Title: Remove the PC Latency permission?
Pcl.Dialog.Enable.Body1: ReLimiter v4 can show NVIDIA PC Latency (PCL) on its overlay, the delay from your input to the frame on screen. Windows only lets it read that when your account is in the Performance Log Users group.
Pcl.Dialog.Enable.Body2: This adds your Windows account to that group. It applies to your whole account, not just ReLimiter: any program you run will be able to record Windows performance data, which normally needs admin rights.
Pcl.Dialog.Enable.Body3: Sign out of Windows and back in afterwards for it to take effect. You can remove it here at any time.

Pcl.Dialog.Disable.Body1: This removes your Windows account from the Performance Log Users group. ReLimiter v4 will no longer be able to read PC Latency.
Pcl.Dialog.Disable.Body2: Sign out of Windows and back in afterwards for it to take effect. If another program added you to this group, it loses the permission too.

Texture.Filtering.Tooltip: Texture sharpness settings from NVIDIA Profile Inspector: LOD bias, anisotropic filtering and texture filtering quality.
Texture.LodBias.Tooltip:
Texture LOD bias for this game. Negative values make textures sharper. Use it for games whose DLSS leaves textures blurry because they don't lower their own bias.

A good start is the value marked for your DLSS mode. Too far negative causes shimmering.

RHI also turns on Transparency Supersampling (all), which DX10, DX11 and DX12 games need for the bias to apply, and allows negative bias. Default removes these.
Texture.AnisotropicFiltering.Tooltip: Forces anisotropic filtering, which keeps textures sharp at angles (floors, roads). App Controlled lets the game decide. Works in most DX9 to DX11 games; many DX12 and Vulkan games ignore it.
Texture.Quality.Tooltip: Texture filtering quality. High Quality turns off the driver's filtering shortcuts (and trilinear optimization) for the cleanest textures at a very small cost. Default lets the driver use Quality.
